newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil probe to examine Sao Paulo mayor's accounts.
newsitem.headline: Brazil probe to examine Sao Paulo mayor's accounts.

text.p: Brazilian senators investigating an alleged multi-million-dollar bond scam voted on Friday to sift through the personal finances of embattled Sao Paulo mayor Celso Pitta and dozens of other officials.

Senators said the decision to overrule Brazil's normally strict bank secrecy laws would reveal whether Pitta, the mayor of South America's largest city, and the other officials under scrutiny had personally benefitted from the alleged scam. Pitta has denied he acted irregularly.

Friday's decision also showed the probe was not subject to political pressures, as had been suggested, lawmakers said. "What people said would not happen has now happened," Sen. Roberto Requiao, a leading member of the investigation, said.

Senators have been investigating since December an alleged racket involving state and municipal debt believed to have been sold at below market rates and then traded for quick profit. Broking houses and officials are accused of sharing the gains.
Several states and municipalities are under investigation but most attention has been focused on Pitta, who was finance secretary of the Sao Paulo municipality when the suspect bonds were issued.
